title: Why leaves change color
text: Today let's look at why leaves change color in the fall. During spring and summer, leaves are green because they contain a lot of chlorophyll, the chemical plants use to capture sunlight. But leaves also contain yellow and orange pigments. We just can't see them, because the green is so strong. In autumn, as days get shorter, trees stop making chlorophyll. The green fades, and the yellow and orange that were there all along finally show through. Red is a little different. Many trees actually produce new red pigments in the fall, possibly to protect their leaves from sunlight while they pull nutrients back into the branches.

title: The Silk Road
text: When we hear Silk Road, we might picture a single road from China to Europe. In fact, it was a network of many routes, over land and sea, used for more than a thousand years. Few traders traveled the whole distance. Instead, goods passed from merchant to merchant, city to city. And silk was only one of many products. Spices, paper, glass, horses and precious metals all moved along these routes. Perhaps most important, so did ideas. Religions, scientific knowledge and technologies such as papermaking spread along the same paths as the goods.

title: Supply and demand
text: Let's start with a simple example. Imagine a new phone becomes very popular. Many people want it, but the factory can only make so many each month. What happens to the price? It goes up, because buyers compete for a limited supply. Now imagine the factory doubles its output. Suddenly there are more phones than buyers at the old price, so sellers lower the price to attract customers. This is the basic idea of supply and demand. When demand rises faster than supply, prices rise. When supply rises faster than demand, prices fall.
